search_log: Searched “David Baldacci First Family excerpt first chapter”; found and opened the sustained NPR/VPM prologue-and-Chapter-1 excerpt and the BingeBooks early-chapter sample.
Searched “First Family David Baldacci point of view third person narrator” and exact-title variants; results about other Baldacci novels and generic POV pages were rejected as non-book-specific.

Searched official Hachette, David Baldacci, Google Books, Barnes & Noble, and Open Library variants; the Hachette page verified the edition, while Google Books, Barnes & Noble, and Open Library previews were bibliographic or inaccessible rather than additional diagnostic prose.

Searched exact-title combinations with “epistolary,” “diary,” “letters,” “multiple narrators,” and “alternating point of view”; no credible source indicated first-person documents or sustained changes of grammatical person.

Reviewed AudioFile, Publishers Weekly, and reader-review results; references to multiple characters, passages, or the kidnapper’s point of view described focalization or audiobook performance, not narrative person, so they were not treated as supporting evidence.
person_note: The base narrator is nonparticipating and consistently uses third person while focalization shifts among characters such as Michelle, Jane, Sean, the president, and others. The authorized opening independently establishes this pattern, and scattered interior Goodreads passages—especially q00491, q00494, and q00503—corroborate it. First-person forms in the quote set are confined to dialogue, while generic “you” statements are gnomic rather than second-person narration. The apparent free-indirect fragments in q00508 are explicitly located within Michelle’s third-person prologue scene by the web excerpt. The main limitation is that the sustained web prose covers the opening and early chapters rather than the entire novel, but the distributed quote evidence and targeted structure searches reveal no contrary or alternating person.
